title: The backlog shape
description: The one backlog.json shape of the requirements-pipeline skill, at workareas/<workarea>/backlog.json. DISTIL writes it, `tim backlog check` validates it against this file, and BUILD and the increment build loop read it. Each row is a requirement (what, why and acceptance), never a recipe, and a full-stack slice, never one layer. The judgement rules a schema cannot hold are in SHAPE.md beside this file.

generatedFrom.description: The source ids the backlog was distilled from, such as ["trace:iuu", "confluence:6518997286"].

invariants.description: Rules every increment must keep, such as "Every page round-trips the CSRF token.". Written once here, not repeated on each row. The loop's planner and reviewers read the envelope as well as the row.

repos.description: Where the programme builds: each repo key a row's `repos` names (any lower-case words, under either lifecycle, such as frontend, backend and tests, or perftests, stub and gateway) mapped to its workspace path and GitHub slug, such as { "frontend": { "path": "repos/trade-imports-plants-frontend", "github": "DEFRA/trade-imports-plants-frontend" } }. The key workspace, at path ".", is the workspace repo itself, such as { "workspace": { "path": ".", "github": "DEFRA/trade-imports-workspace", "requireApproval": true } }. DISTIL works it out from the goal and writes it here, so BUILD passes it to the loop as its `repos` arg without asking anyone. Older backlogs leave it out, and BUILD asks.

themes.description: The groups the rows build in, so each group builds on its own machine and branch without conflicting pull requests. DISTIL writes it when sources.json has `themes`. A theme's boundary is drawn by the code it touches: no two themes touch the same path. Every `todo` or `blocked` row names one in its `theme`. `tim backlog split` writes one backlog per theme from it. The rules a schema cannot check are in SHAPE.md.

splitOff.description: The themes split off this backlog early by `tim backlog split <workarea> --theme <id> --write`, one pointer each. A theme split off is no longer in `themes`, and none of its rows is in `increments`: they live only in its own backlog, built on its own branch. A re-distil carries this list over unchanged, except that it may add to a pointer's `pickUp`, and never drafts a row for a requirement a pointer holds. `tim distil coverage` counts each such requirement as covered by the split backlog. The rules a schema cannot check are in SHAPE.md.

theme.description: Split backlogs only: the id of the theme this backlog builds, written by `tim backlog split`. Every row here belongs to it. A split backlog also carries `branch` and `parent`, and never `themes`.

branch.description: Split backlogs only: the branch the theme builds on, such as "feat/NO_JIRA-hrp-origin-and-commodity-origin-pages". `tim backlog split` writes it: `feat/NO_JIRA-<programme>-<theme id>` unless given another prefix. Every repo the theme touches uses the same name.

parent.description: Split backlogs only: where the theme came from and when it lands, written by `tim backlog split`, such as { "workarea": "shared/hrp", "wave": 2, "landsAfter": ["origin-pages"] }.

workarea.description: The workarea of the backlog it was split from, such as "shared/hrp". Re-distil and re-split there, never here.

wave.description: Its place in the landing order: 1 lands first. Themes in the same wave have no ordering need between them, so they build in parallel.

landsAfter.description: The theme ids it depends on: the themes whose rows its rows wait for. [] when it waits for none.

touches.description: Split backlogs only: the code areas the theme owns, copied from its entry in the parent's `themes`, such as ["frontend:src/server/origin"]. The plan keeps the theme's changes inside them.

increments.description: The rows, in build order. `tim backlog next` returns the first one that is not withheld and whose every dependency is done.

themeId.description: A theme id: lower-case words joined by hyphens, such as "origin-pages".

touch.description: A code area: a repo key from the envelope's `repos`, a colon, then a path prefix inside that repo, such as "frontend:src/server/origin" or "tests:tests/plants/origin". A path of "." means the whole repo.

theme.description: One theme: a group of rows that touch the same code and nobody else's.

id.description: Stable once rows are built in it: its split backlog's workarea and branch are named by it.

title.description: What the theme builds, in plain English.

why.description: The evidence for the boundary: the code its rows' requirements touch, and why no other theme touches it.

touches.description: The code areas the theme owns. No path here is inside, or the same as, another theme's path in the same repo.

dependsOn.description: Theme ids that must land first, because one of this theme's rows depends on one of theirs, in `themes` or in `splitOff`. [] when it waits for none.

splitOffTheme.description: A pointer to a theme split off early, written by `tim backlog split --theme`. Everything but `pickUp` is fixed once written.

theme.description: The theme's id, as it was in `themes`.

title.description: The theme's title, as it was in `themes`.

why.description: The theme's why, as it was in `themes`.

touches.description: The code areas the theme owns, as they were in `themes`. No theme left in `themes` may touch them, and a re-distil hands a new requirement that changes them to this theme's `pickUp`.

dependsOn.description: The theme ids it lands after, as they were in `themes`. Each must stay named in `themes` or `splitOff` under that id: `tim backlog check` refuses one that is not. A theme left in `themes` may depend on this one.

branch.description: The branch the theme builds on, the same as its split backlog's `branch`, such as "feat/NO_JIRA-hrp-origin-pages".

workarea.description: The split backlog's workarea, such as "shared/hrp/themes/origin-pages": what an `externalDependsOn` on one of its rows names.

backlog.description: The split backlog's path, relative to this backlog's folder, such as "themes/origin-pages/backlog.json".

increments.description: The ids of every row that moved, dropped, rejected and merged rows included. No row here may reuse one.

requirements.description: The requirement ids the moved rows that cover (todo, blocked, done, deferred) covered, from their `requirements`. `tim distil coverage` counts each as covered by the split backlog.

fingerprints.description: Each of those requirements' fingerprint in distil/requirements.json when the theme was split off: a sha256 of its statement, status, delta, delta note, blocker and conflicts. `tim distil coverage` names a requirement whose fingerprint has since changed, so the report can hand the change to the split branch. Left out when the workarea had no requirements.json.

pickUp.description: Requirement ids a later re-distil adopted that fall in this theme's `touches`. The consolidator writes them here instead of drafting a row, and the report hands them to the split branch, which adds rows for them in its own backlog. `tim distil coverage` counts each as covered by the split backlog.

at.description: When the theme was split off, as an ISO 8601 time, such as "2026-10-09T14:30:00.000Z".

externalDependency.description: A row in another workarea's backlog that must be `done` first.

workarea.description: The other backlog's workarea, such as "shared/hrp/themes/origin-pages".

id.description: The row's id in that backlog.

text.description: Text that is not empty or only whitespace.

repo.description: One repo the programme builds in.

path.description: The repo's folder, relative to the workspace root, such as "repos/trade-imports-plants-frontend", or "." for the workspace repo itself. tim knows the workspace repo by the folder name trade-imports-workspace, wherever it is cloned: gates.json keys its rungs by it.

github.description: The repo's GitHub owner/name, such as "DEFRA/trade-imports-plants-frontend". Taken from the repo's origin remote.

requireApproval.description: true when a person must approve the repo's pull request before the loop merges it, such as for the workspace repo, whose changes steer every later run. Left out, or false, the loop merges on green as usual. `tim build start` lists the repos it is true for in its result's requireApproval.

increment.description: One increment: a requirement (what, why and acceptance), never a recipe, and a full-stack slice covering every repo the behaviour needs. The build loop's plan stage works out the how against the live tree, just in time, and writes it to workareas/<workarea>/plans/<id>.md. Other fields are allowed, because older backlogs carry more.

id.description: `inc-NNN`. Stable: never renumber, because rulings and commits cite it.

detail.description: What and why: the user need, and the behaviour afterwards.

acceptanceCriteria.description: At least one outcome a user, operator, other system or reviewer can observe. Each may end with its provenance in brackets, such as "(confluence:6518997286 §3)". What a criterion may and must not name is in SHAPE.md.

dependsOn.description: Ids that must be `done` first. A real ordering need, not a layer order. [] when it waits for nothing.

externalDependsOn.description: Rows in other workareas' backlogs that must be `done` first, such as [{ "workarea": "shared/hrp/themes/origin-pages", "id": "inc-003" }]. `tim backlog split` writes it from a dependsOn on a row in another theme. `tim backlog next` reads each one's status in its own backlog.

theme.description: The id of the theme the row belongs to, one of the envelope's `themes`, or the envelope's `theme` in a split backlog. Required of every `todo` or `blocked` row once the backlog has themes.

status.description: `todo` is buildable. `done` is what a dependency waits for. `blocked`, `deferred`, `dropped`, `rejected` and `merged-into` are withheld: `tim backlog next` never picks them up.

repos.description: The repo keys the slice touches, such as ["backend", "tests", "frontend"]: keys of the envelope's `repos`, in merge order, provider before consumer: a service before the frontend that calls it, a stub before the service that calls it, a tests or performance-tests repo after every service it exercises. The full lifecycle merges in this order unless the keys are exactly frontend, backend and tests, which always merge backend, tests, frontend. Left out, the loop takes every configured repo. [] means the row changes no backlog repo, such as a docs row whose output is in the workspace repo; only the branch lifecycle builds one.

sources.description: Where it came from, such as { "source": "trace:iuu", "ref": "pages/transport-details.json" }.

requirements.description: The distiller's requirement ids the row covers, such as "req-004", from distil/requirements.json.

openQuestions.description: What is still undecided. A `blocked` row must have at least one. A `todo` row may carry one that has a default, which the builder follows and says so.

notes.description: Anything a builder should know that is not a requirement, such as which slices the row combines and why. Text, or a list of text: `tim backlog set --note` appends.

gate.description: A checkpoint: the loop lands this increment, then stops so a person can look before anything that depends on it. The text says what to look at. null means no checkpoint.

merge.description: Branch lifecycle only: a ref to merge into each named repo before the row is built, such as { "tests": "origin/main" }. The loop fetches and runs `git merge --no-ff --no-commit <ref>`, the implementor resolves the merge by the plan, and the land stage commits it as a two-parent merge commit. Every key must be in the row's `repos`. null or absent: no merge. The full lifecycle ignores it.

gatePhases.description: Branch lifecycle only: the phases of `tim build gate` the baseline and the ladder run for this row, such as ["unit", "fit"] for a merge row whose end-to-end proof is another row's. [] runs no gate phase, for a row that changes no backlog repo. null or absent: all three. The full lifecycle always runs all three.

awaitCi.description: Branch lifecycle only: false pushes the row and records its pull requests without waiting for CI, for a row whose pull requests cannot run checks yet (GitHub runs none on a pull request that conflicts with its base). null or absent: true. The full lifecycle always waits.

ticket.description: Written by the build loop through `tim backlog set --ticket`: the Jira key raised for the increment.

branch.description: Written by the build loop through `tim backlog set --branch`: the branch the increment builds on.

commit.description: Written by the build loop through `tim backlog set --commit`: the commit the increment landed as.

prs.description: Written by the build loop through `tim backlog set --pr`: the increment's pull requests, one per repo, merged into by url.

not.description: Recipe fields. A row says what, why and acceptance; the build plans the how just in time.

then.description: A blocked row says what it waits for.
